_comment: SkillSpector suppressions for this repo, passed to the scanner with --baseline by
the skill-scan skill's scripts/skill-scan.mjs. Discipline lives in skill-maintainer's
references/standards.md: an entry is added only on the operator's word, is scoped as
narrowly as its cause with a LITERAL matcher, and its reason carries a 'Still flag
Adjudicated finding by finding in issue 62. Three sections:
rules[]       - findings the scanner reports, suppressed by literal id+path
coverage[]    - files the scanner could not finish reading. NOT a finding, and
the scanner's own baseline cannot express it; this section is
read by our guard only. Accepting one does not accept another:
a skill still blocks if any unread file is unaccounted for.

rules.reason: conventions.md documents the workflow's own comment protocol - the '<!-- vsk:v1 type=... -->' marker every artifact opens with - so a scanner looking for instructions hidden in HTML comments matches the documentation of the mechanism, not an instance of it. The markers are metadata read by guard scripts, carry no imperative, and the file is shared by ten skills, which is why one cause produces ten findings. Still flag if: a marker example gains text addressed to the agent rather than key=value metadata, or the pattern appears in a file that is not documenting the protocol.

The brief template shows the same '<!-- vsk:v1 type=brief ... -->' marker an issue body must open with, inside a fenced markdown block that a reader copies. It is an example of the protocol above, in the one file whose job is to show it. Still flag if: the template's HTML comments gain prose addressed to the agent rather than key=value metadata.

The template opens with '<!-- vsk-dev:start -->', the delimiter dev-setup uses to find and re-render the one block of AGENTS.md it owns. It is a machine-readable boundary marker, deliberately invisible in rendered markdown, and dev-setup would be unable to edit idempotently without it. Still flag if: the delimiter comment gains content beyond the marker itself, or a second unexplained comment appears in the template.

harness-facts.md documents how each harness discovers skills, including Claude Code's '@path/to/file' import syntax and the HTML-comment source citations ('<!-- source: CLAUDE-CODE-SKILLS -->') that tie every normative sentence to the page it came from. A scanner reading a file that explains agent-file mechanics will match the mechanics being explained. Still flag if: a citation comment stops naming a source and starts containing instructions, or an import example is written as something to execute rather than to recognise.

standards.md carries the same '<!-- source: ... -->' citation comments, which are how a reader tells a verified normative sentence from commentary and how the weekly refresh knows which sentences a drifted source invalidates. Removing them would make the freshness contract unauditable. Still flag if: a source comment carries anything but a source identifier, or an uncited HTML comment appears among the normative sentences.

authoring.md marks the tables it mirrors from skill-maintainer's standards with '<!-- mirrored -->' so the refresh runner knows which copies must move together. It is a synchronisation marker between two files, not an instruction. Still flag if: a mirrored marker gains prose, or the comment appears on content that is not actually mirrored elsewhere.

Every refresh contract carries HTML comments naming which reference sections a drifted source invalidates - the mapping the refresh runner reads to build its PR. It is machine-readable bookkeeping about this repo's own files. Scope of what this hides, stated plainly: the path matches the refresh contract of ALL twelve skills, while only three report the finding today; a hidden instruction added to any skill's REFRESH.md would be silenced by this rule. It is written this way because the contracts share one authored format and one purpose, and per-skill rules would drift apart. Still flag if: a comment in a refresh contract addresses the agent directly rather than naming an affected file or section.

fingerprints.reason: skillify only. RA1 (Rogue Agent / self-modification) is CORRECT about the pattern and is accepted with its limits stated, not explained away: this refresh contract instructs an agent to rewrite skillify's own marked sections when upstream sources drift. What actually bounds it, verified: refresh work runs on refresh/** branches, and .github/workflows/refresh-guard.yml fails any such PR whose diff touches anything outside a skill's refresh/ directory - so the automated path cannot reach skillify's SKILL.md or references at all. Checksums, versions and timestamps in refresh/sources.json are runner-only by repo rule, and the workflow maintains one standing PR rather than pushing. What bounds it as of 01-09-2026: the default branch IS branch-protected - a PR is required, force-pushes and deletion are blocked, and admins are not exempt - so 'a human reviews before merge' is now an enforced control rather than a convention. This sentence previously recorded the opposite, and the protection was enabled because this suppression depended on a control that did not exist. Still narrower than it sounds: refresh-guard only constrains refresh/** branches, so an agent following this contract from any other branch is bounded by the PR requirement alone. The residual risk is therefore real but not unique to this contract: it is the same risk carried by any agent with write access to the repository, and the finding is accepted on that basis rather than on a control that does not exist. Still flag if: this contract's wording changes at all (content-hashed, so it re-triggers automatically), or refresh-guard.yml stops restricting refresh/** diffs to refresh/ directories - that guard is the one real bound named here. Re-adjudicated 03-09-2026 (#101) after REFRESH.md dropped the authoring.md mirrored-table bullet (that table is now a citation of skill-maintainer's Hard limits): the hashed instruction - update skillify's marked section on a normal branch when skill-maintainer's sources drift - is the same sentence with 'two marked sections' read 'marked section', refresh-guard.yml is unchanged, and only the digest moves.

coverage.reason: The scanner reports static_parse_limit on this file and degrades 1 static analyzer(s) for the whole skill. What is established: the degradation is the scanner's bounded shell parser giving up, not a property of this file's behaviour - a control experiment isolated one trigger, a JavaScript template literal in assignment position, which degrades a two-line file while forty template literals inside function calls do not degrade at all. What is NOT established: that this is the trigger in this particular file. The specific span was not isolated per file, and this acceptance does not claim it was. It is accepted because the alternative is banning ordinary syntax from every skill that ships a script, and because the acceptance is bound to this file's exact contents - any edit drops it and forces re-adjudication. Still flag if: the reported reason code changes from static_parse_limit, or the number of degraded analyzers rises above 1 - either means a cause other than the one accepted here. Re-adjudicated 03-09-2026 (#107) after preflight.mjs gained the ready-issue assignee warning: the change adds one warn branch over an array already read two lines above, and only the digest moves. The full dev-implement scan now lists thirteen degraded analyzers against this file, which reads like the Still-flag clause firing; it is not. A one-file probe (this file plus SKILL.md alone, scanned with --no-provision) reproduces exactly static_parse_limit and exactly one degraded analyzer, static_patterns_tool_misuse. The other twelve are scripts/reclaim.mjs's already-accepted obfuscated_instruction_text, which the guard attributes to every partly-inspected file in the skill — the same aggregation already recorded on scripts/evidence-upload.mjs's entry. The clause is measured against the isolated file, and against that it holds.

Accepts the eight AE1 findings on this file. AE1 is a completeness signal reported through the findings channel - the scanner's own text is 'Referenced artifact was not completely inspected' - so it is accepted here rather than as a rule or fingerprint. Two traced causes: this SKILL.md cites repo-root paths (packages/cli/packaging.json, packages/cli/scripts/validate-skill.mjs, CONTRIBUTING.md, .vegastack/dev.md) that cannot resolve relative to a skill directory and are correct for a skill whose subject is this repository; and it links to references/standards.md, which the parser cannot finish for the reason on that file's own entry. Not a rule, because {id: AE1, path: SKILL.md} silences this in all twelve skills and demonstrably hid a real regression when tried. Not fingerprints, because the scanner emits eight location-bound hashes while its own generator deduplicates them to two, so a fingerprint set provably cannot cover them. Scope of what this hides: any AE1 on this one file. Still flag if: this file changes at all - the sha256 above drops the acceptance automatically - or a rule id other than AE1 appears here, which this acceptance does not cover and which will still block. Accepts the reduced coverage on this file: SkillSpector 2.11.0 reports obfuscated_instruction_text (degrading 13 static analyzers for the whole skill) and static_parse_limit (1 more) on it. CAUSE, isolated on 01-09-2026 rather than assumed - single-construct probes scanned as one-file skills: the control-character regex in safe() scans COMPLETE (it was the first suspect and it is not the trigger); a JavaScript template literal in assignment position reproduces static_parse_limit on a two-line file, which is the identical, already-adjudicated trigger behind the coverage acceptances on preflight.mjs, ship-gate.mjs, status.mjs and scaffold-skill.mjs (issue 62); obfuscated_instruction_text did not reproduce from the git URL, the fetch-with-headers block, or the upgrade command table in isolation, and did not reproduce from either half of the file alone - it emerges from the whole file, exactly as it already does on ship-gate.mjs, whose accepted reason names the same pair of codes. WHAT BOUNDS THE RISK, because this file is the one that adds auto-install and a network call and the security axis was right to say that is the worst place to lose analyzers: every command is an execFileSync argument array with no shell and no interpolation; the only network call is a fixed GET to a hard-coded api.github.com releases URL whose result is regex-validated and used solely to print a version string; the sole install source is NVIDIA's own repository; all command output is sanitized through safe() before it reaches a terminal; and the whole file is unit-tested through injected runners. Still flag if: this file gains a new outbound destination or a URL that is assembled at runtime or read from configuration, gains any shell execution or string-interpolated command, learns to install from a source other than NVIDIA's repository, or begins writing outside the operator's own user account. The sha256 binds this acceptance to the file as adjudicated - any edit expires it and forces re-adjudication. The scanner reports obfuscated_instruction_text, static_parse_limit on this file and degrades 13 static analyzer(s) for the whole skill. Adjudicated 02-09-2026 (#90) when reclaim.mjs was added: isolated by a one-file probe reproducing both reason codes and 13 degraded analyzers - the same pair and count already accepted on ship-gate.mjs, whose reason this mirrors. The 13-analyzer blindness is real and called out: prompt injection, privilege escalation, supply chain, rogue agent, SSRF and others do not complete on this file. WHAT BOUNDS THE RISK: reclaim.mjs is a first-party, operator-run guard whose whole diff is reviewed on every change; every gh call is an execFileSync argument array with no shell and no string interpolation; the commands are fixed (issue edit --remove-label/--add-label/--remove-assignee, issue comment) and target exactly the one issue named on the CLI; the login it unassigns is read from that issue's own assignees; it writes nothing outside the operator's own gh auth; the read-verify (evaluateReclaim) is unit-tested through injected inputs; and it refuses a ledger fresher than the orphan threshold unless --force. The honest difference from ship-gate.mjs, which this acceptance does NOT hide: reclaim.mjs MUTATES remote state (a label swap, an unassign, a comment) where ship-gate only reads and runs the check command - re-adjudicate this one first if that mutation surface changes. Still flag if: this file gains string-interpolated or shell commands, a new outbound destination, writes to any issue other than the one passed on its CLI or to anything outside the operator's account, or the number of degraded analyzers rises above 13. The sha256 binds this acceptance to the file as adjudicated - any edit expires it and forces re-adjudication.
